Maya Chen: Heads-up — I ran a quick perf pass on the INT8 weight-only pack path (AWQ) on dedicated tonight and confirmed a 18-25% tail latency regression for small chat requests when KV cache hits are common. attaching notes.
Liam O'Connor: ugh, is this the packing hotpath or kernel selection? any changes since yesterday's deploy?
Maya Chen: looks like packing + calibration interplay. When group-size changes during on-the-fly calibration we occasionally emit slightly different alignment bytes which trips the packer into a slower fallback path.
Sofia Patel: can you paste the profile? small examples help.
Maya Chen: pasted below — notable things: pack_unaligned() spikes, then a long memcpy in slab_eviction(), and a kernel chooser that falls back from int8-fast-v2 -> int8-serial.
Maya Chen: ```
# perf sample (summary)
25.4%  runtime        [.] pack_unaligned
13.1%  alloc          [.] slab_eviction
10.6%  runtime        [.] kernel_select_slow
 9.2%  llc_miss       [.] kv_cache_lookup
```
Devon: hmm slab_eviction during small chats suggests pack buffer churn. How often are we flushing prefixes? batching heuristics maybe small group sizes causing more pack/unpack cycles.
Maya Chen: exactly. On traces where KV hit ratio > 60% we still see repeated pack/unpack because the pack key (prefix hash + calib id) mutates when calibration updates the per-group scales.
Liam O'Connor: so calibration is non-deterministic across mini-rollouts and changes pack signatures -> cache misses -> pack allocation. Is this a calibration jitter issue or pack key construction bug?
Sofia Patel: could be both. I think our pack key embeds a float32 checksum of per-group quant params; small nondeterminism will alter it. We should normalize/calib-quantize to fixed ints for the key.
Devon: low-effort mitigation: add a short grace period where calibration updates don't change the pack key for active sessions (eg 5s), so in-flight KV hits stay sticky.
Maya Chen: tried a local patch that hashes quant params after rounding to 8-bit signed ints; tail latency dropped back to baseline in my microbench. will run full regression.
Liam O'Connor: nice. Any kernel regressions? the log mentions fallback to int8-serial; why did kernel chooser pick serial instead of fast-v2?
Maya Chen: fast-v2 requires contiguous 16-byte aligned groups. When packer emitted padded layout due to misaligned groups the kernel capability check rejects it. That is the real perf cliff.
Sofia Patel: so two-pronged fix: (1) stabilize pack key by quantizing/calib-normalizing before hashing, (2) make kernel capability check less brittle by accepting padded layout and handling it in fast path (or provide a fast padded kernel).
Devon: agree. Also add telemetry: emit tags on requests indicating pack_key_version + kernel_choice so we can correlate tail spikes in Console.
Maya Chen: created a tiny TODO list in the test matrix:
- [ ] add deterministic pack-key normalization (round quant params -> int8)
- [ ] add grace-window for calib updates for active sessions
- [ ] add fast-padded kernel prototype (eng-runtime)
- [ ] instrument per-request pack_key & kernel_choice in logs/console
- [ ] run 24h soak with KV hit > 70% workload
Liam O'Connor: timeline?
Maya Chen: I'll PR the pack-key normalization today, grace-window tomorrow. Devon can prototype the telemetry tag. Sofia will own kernel work with eng-runtime.
infra-bot: Deploy patch branch/redwood/pack-key-normalize to staging at 2026-03-18T02:20Z (build #4127). :rocket:
Devon: I'll run a staging soak after the deploy and post the smoke numbers. if all green, we can roll to dedicated low-rpm nodes first.
Sofia Patel: also pinging @eng-runtime to review fast-padded kernel feasibility. we might prefer adding a light-weight path rather than widening checks.
Maya Chen: thanks team. I'll attach the microbench script in a follow-up. short-term both fixes together look safe and address the KV leakage -> pack churn -> kernel fallback cascade. :thumbsup:
